name: Draft Gmail support replies with an AI agent that asks for review
description: For each new email in Gmail, an AI agent reads the thread, drafts a reply and asks a person to review it with the Request Approval tool, in the middle of its own reasoning. The reviewer can edit the draft and approve it, or reject it with a note, and the agent continues with that answer: it sends the approved text, or rewrites the draft from the note and asks again. Questions the agent cannot answer from the thread go to the reviewer in the same form.
shortDescription: An AI agent drafts support replies, asks a person to review them mid-conversation and keeps working with the feedback.
keyFeatures: Request Approval attached to the AI Agent as a tool, so the agent decides when to ask and reads the answer
The review form carries the agent's draft as an editable field and any question it has for the reviewer
Rejections with a note send the agent back to revise, for up to three review rounds in one run
The agent sends the reviewer's approved text itself with the Gmail Send Reply tool
prerequisites: Google Mail (Gmail) connection for the support inbox
Someone who answers reviews in the Approval Tasks inbox, or swap the Approval Task channel for Slack, email or another channel
Server public URL configured, so the review links can be generated
Sending only after approval is an instruction to the agent, not enforced by the platform; use the approval gate template when every send must be blocked until approved
idealFor: Support teams that want to coach an AI agent reply by reply, editing its drafts and answering its questions, without leaving the review form.
steps: Trigger: poll Gmail for a new email.
Draft and review: the AI Agent reads the thread and the sender's earlier emails, drafts a reply and calls Request Approval; the run pauses on a review form with the draft.
Approved: the agent sends the reviewer's version of the reply in the original thread.
Rejected with a note: the agent rewrites the draft from the note and asks for review again, at most three rounds.
Log outcome: whether a reply was sent, and the agent's summary, is logged.
